title: Association between alcohol and cardiovascular disease: Mendelian randomisation analysis based on individual participant data
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To use the rs1229984 variant in the alcohol dehydrogenase 1B gene (ADH1B) as an instrument to investigate the causal role of alcohol in cardiovascular disease. DESIGN: Mendelian randomisation meta-analysis of 56 epidemiological studies. PARTICIPANTS: 261 991 individuals of European descent, including 20 259 coronary heart disease cases and 10 164 stroke events. Data were available on ADH1B rs1229984 variant, alcohol phenotypes, and cardiovascular biomarkers. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Odds ratio for coronary heart disease and stroke associated with the ADH1B variant in all individuals and by categories of alcohol consumption. RESULTS: Carriers of the A-allele of ADH1B rs1229984 consumed 17.2% fewer units of alcohol per week (95% confidence interval 15.6% to 18.9%), had a lower prevalence of binge drinking (odds ratio 0.78 (95% CI 0.73 to 0.84)), and had higher abstention (odds ratio 1.27 (1.21 to 1.34)) than non-carriers. Rs1229984 A-allele carriers had lower systolic blood pressure (-0.88 (-1.19 to -0.56) mm Hg), interleukin-6 levels (-5.2% (-7.8 to -2.4%)), waist circumference (-0.3 (-0.6 to -0.1) cm), and body mass index (-0.17 (-0.24 to -0.10) kg/m(2)). Rs1229984 A-allele carriers had lower odds of coronary heart disease (odds ratio 0.90 (0.84 to 0.96)). The protective association of the ADH1B rs1229984 A-allele variant remained the same across all categories of alcohol consumption (P=0.83 for heterogeneity). Although no association of rs1229984 was identified with the combined subtypes of stroke, carriers of the A-allele had lower odds of ischaemic stroke (odds ratio 0.83 (0.72 to 0.95)). CONCLUSIONS: Individuals with a genetic variant associated with non-drinking and lower alcohol consumption had a more favourable cardiovascular profile and a reduced risk of coronary heart disease than those without the genetic variant. This suggests that reduction of alcohol consumption, even for light to moderate drinkers, is beneficial for cardiovascular health.

claims.text: Carriers of the ADH1B rs1229984 A-allele consumed 17.2% fewer units of alcohol per week compared to non-carriers.
Carriers of the ADH1B rs1229984 A-allele had lower odds of binge drinking compared to non-carriers.
Carriers of the ADH1B rs1229984 A-allele had higher odds of alcohol abstention compared to non-carriers.
Carriers of the ADH1B rs1229984 A-allele had lower systolic blood pressure compared to non-carriers.
Carriers of the ADH1B rs1229984 A-allele had lower interleukin-6 levels compared to non-carriers.
Carriers of the ADH1B rs1229984 A-allele had lower waist circumference compared to non-carriers.
Carriers of the ADH1B rs1229984 A-allele had lower body mass index compared to non-carriers.
Carriers of the ADH1B rs1229984 A-allele had lower odds of coronary heart disease compared to non-carriers.
Carriers of the ADH1B rs1229984 A-allele had lower odds of ischaemic stroke compared to non-carriers.
Carriers of the ADH1B rs1229984 A-allele showed no association with combined subtypes of stroke.
Carriers of the ADH1B rs1229984 A-allele showed no overall association with type 2 diabetes.
Carriers of the ADH1B rs1229984 A-allele showed no overall difference in HDL cholesterol concentration compared to non-carriers.

limitations.text: Existing experimental studies on the HDL cholesterol raising effect of alcohol may be prone to bias due to small sample size and short follow-up.
Self-reported questionnaires make it difficult to correctly classify long-term non-drinkers in observational studies.
Reduced statistical power to detect a stronger protective association of coronary heart disease in heavy drinkers due to the low number of events in the heavy drinking stratum.
Relatively small number of stroke events and the use of combined stroke subtypes, which could have obscured differential associations by pathological or aetiological subtype.

future_work.text: Access large-scale population studies such as UK Biobank and China Kadoorie Biobank Study to minimize measurement error in alcohol exposure, provide sufficient coronary heart disease events, and enable detailed examination of stroke subtypes.

methodologies.name: Mendelian randomisation meta-analysis
methodologies.description: Used the ADH1B rs1229984 genetic variant as an instrumental variable to examine causal associations between alcohol intake, cardiovascular biomarkers, and cardiovascular outcomes using pooled individual participant data.

conditions: Dominant genetic model (rs1229984 A-allele carriers vs non-carriers)
